jobs.company: Eurofins US Food, Feed, & Supplement Testing
jobs.title: Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate.

The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in agroscience Contract Research Organisation services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialised and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products.

In over 30 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to 58,000 staff across a decentralised and entrepreneurial network of 900 laboratories in over 54 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.

Eurofins Assurance offers third-party certification and supply chain compliance services across North America, helping the Food, Dietary Supplements, Cosmetics, OTC drugs industries meet the requirements of retailers, brands and consumers, facilitating international trade. Eurofins Assurance certification also helps companies demonstrate regulatory compliance, commitment to best practices, and to continuously improve.

Job Description

To work as part of the Operations Team providing a high level of professional customer service to our clients. Responsible to be knowledgeable of program area requirements, to ensure proper application of program operational rules, and to implement efficient planning, coordination and execution for all certification and 2nd Party Audits across the assigned program area/s. To be the main contact for clients of the assigned program area, ensuring operational compliance with all program and accreditation requirements.

Program Coordinator Duties Include but are not Limited to the Following:

Delivering Excellent Customer Service for clients and contractors. Main contact for external stakeholders, including clients and external scheme owners. Coordinate and arrange audits, oversee execution of certification and 2nd party audit processes end-to-end in line with the requirements of the applicable program and ISO 17065 requirements. Coordinate and oversee execution of accreditation and witness audits for all programs. Maintain up to date, working knowledge of program operational requirements and contribute to process improvements and changes to ensure delivery of efficient and compliant certification services. Attend meetings and conferences as required by Certification Program Owners (CPO) or support the business at trade events.

Liaison with CPOs /
Preparation and issue of Audit application forms and contracts to new and existing clients
Liaison with clients to arrange dates for audit visits to maintain Certification status in ADVANCE of their audit window and the subsequent communication with auditors
Liaison with auditors regarding booked audits (Employed and Subcontractors)
Maintaining and updating Audit scheduling systems
Managing the audit diary effectively and efficiently to ensure optimum Auditor utilisation and minimise audit delivery costs
Liaison with GRMA / ANAB / SSCI or technical manager to assist the planning of Compliance and witness audits and support maintainenance of witness records
Ensure assignment of audits to auditors with correct skill categories
Maintain log of all lost and gained sites, including reasons for leaving (where applicable) and contact details – communicate all losses and gains to Sales / Account manager for follow up
Ensure Sales is advised of any potential new clients for follow up
Maintain an up to date list of all clients including address, contact details and Job Title of key personnel, ensuring ADMS is updated accordingly
Ensure all key communication with sites is saved in the client files
Support continuous improvement of systems and ways of working including defining system enhancement requests for Eurofins Assurance Online (EAOL) or other supporting software
Document all client info within the audit system – to include all 2nd Party clients as well as external scheme clients
Generate Standard operating procedures (SOPs) for EAOL and Eurofins Assurance US systems
Use and implement of EAOL as certification tool, maintaining accurate data
Follow and document certification processes including uploading of reports, certification decision and certificate generation into EAOL.
Attend & participate in team meetings
Ensure accurate pricing, for efficient invoicing. Including follow up on collection of overdue invoices
Execute withdrawal of certification when payment is not received, or site no longer meets certification requirements
Manage cadence of all surveillance, monitoring, or recertification activities
In addition, any other duties which may reasonably be expected to fall within the scope of this position, as assigned.

Qualifications

Basic Minimum Education Requirements :

Bachelor’s degree in life science, food science/technology, quality, regulatory affairs, data science, engineering, or related area.

Additional work experience can be substituted for education.

Basic Minimum Qualifications :

Minimum 1-3 years of experience
Demonstrated competency with Microsoft Excel, Word, PPT and databases is essential
Commitment to providing Excellent Customer Service is essential
Data management experience a plus
Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship.

The ideal candidate would possess
:

Ability to think on your feet, work well under pressure and a strong urge to get the job done are all essential for this role.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills are essential as is ability to have a flexible attitude to work and the constantly changing demands of the role and the industry.

Additional Information

Position is full-time working remotely Monday - Friday 08:00am - 5:00 pm,
and additional hours as needed.

Excellent full-time benefits including:

Comprehensive medical coverage, dental, and vision options
Life and disability insurance
401(k) with company match
Paid vacation and holidays

jobs.title: Residency Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
This position affords a talented individual the opportunity for professional development to lead and manage the daily operations of the residency/fellowship program ensuring the successful implementation of program objectives. The candidate will be responsible for co-coordinating with the program director the development of program policies, procedures and system processes that are compliant with ACGME guidelines, maintaining databases, recruiting residents, and promoting effective working relationships with faculty, residents, medical affiliates and related professional associations/organizations.

Essential Functions (Principal Duties And Job Responsibilities)

Program Accreditation:
Monitors maintenance of program accreditation with ACGME and CODA.
Prepares and coordinates materials and resources for ACGME site visit reviews. Works with developing, implementing and enforcing program-specific policies as required by the ACGME, CODA and other accrediting bodies in conjunction with the program director.
Reviews and assesses current program and institutional requirements for the program; monitors requirement for updates; works with program director in implementation; and completes all required updates on the ACGME and CODA websites.
Monitors resident compliance with completion of ACGME and CODA surveys to ensure required compliance rate is reached. Works with the program director and faculty in planning, developing and implementing program’s quality improvement activities.
Maintains and monitors information in WebADs and other specialty-specific electronic databases, including but not limited to, program attrition, program characteristics, scholarly activity, board pass rates, case logs, residents and faculty surveys, milestones reporting and annual program updates.
Coordinates and facilitates scheduled meetings with faculty, residents, and site directors regarding the program, including Clinical Competency Committee and the annual program evaluation.
Develops and ensures that Program Letters of Agreement are in place for every rotation site and are kept current.
Prepares, monitors and maintains program manuals, reports and residential files, procedure logs, attendance records and other official documentation to ensure trainees meet graduation requirements and program maintains its accreditation status.
Documents verification of training for each trainee as per the requirements of each specialty board. Maintains all current and alumni resident files with documentation as per specific program requirements.
Organizes and gathers required documentation for completing ACGME and CODA self-study and site visits.
Participates on Program Evaluation Committee (PEC) and ensures required documents are available for committee to function.
Monitors specialty boards pass rates for graduates from the program and reports 5-year data as required by ACGME as required by specific program.
Monitors and analyzes data to determine compliance with ACGME and CODA requirements.
Manages and maintains program data in MyEvaluations software, including schedules, conferences, and evaluations.
Rotation and Coverage Schedules (As Required By Specific Program):
Prepares, monitors and disseminates faculty and residential rotations, on-call coverage, work hours and vacation schedules using MyEvaluations software.
Updates, changes, and ensures services are covered appropriately in regards to the rotation and faculty schedules. Arranges appropriate elective and required out rotations for residents/fellows and provides appropriate documents on residency trainees to affiliated hospitals.
Monitors, approves and tracks resident clinical hours and payroll in Banner and MyEvaluations.
Collaborates with the Office of Graduate Medical Education and Finance to reconcile attendance records and resolves discrepancies for accurate IRIS reporting to Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). Prepares FTE budget for Finance.

Lectures And Events (As Required By Specific Program)

Organizes courses, conferences, alumni and graduation events, including journal club, textbook review, didactic lectures, slide review, Grand Rounds and visiting professorships; confirms lecturers and guest speakers; assists with travel and expense reimbursements; publicizes events, manages registration and tracks attendance. Ensures that conferences (lectures, grand rounds etc.) align with established CME guidelines.
Reserve facilities and equipment, arranges catering, transportation and other maintenance issues. Staffs events as needed to ensure a high-quality experience for all participants. Assists the GME Office with system wide orientation event as needed.
Schedules and proctors In-Training Exam.

Evaluation

Monitors evaluation process. Creates evaluation tools and maps evaluations to ACGME milestones under the direction of the program director.
Collects various evaluations on behalf of the house staff when they rotate through the affiliate sites after each rotation (i.e., evaluation of faculty by residents; evaluation of program by faculty and residents; semi-annual evaluations of residents, final written evaluations of graduating residents; evaluations of residents by multiple evaluators. Including patients, medical students, and peers and all other evaluations as required by the individual accreditation program requirements.)
Organizes and prepares PEC meetings. Participates on PEC and documents minutes including action plan as required.
Compiles all required documents to ensure the Clinical Competence Committee (CCC) functions to the Program Requirements and standards of the Next Accreditation System.
Recruitment and Selection:
Manages annual residency and/or fellowship recruitment processes. Updates program recruitment information in the Association of American Medical Colleges’ (AAMC) Fellowship and Residencies Electronic Interactive Database (FREIDA, and the American Dental Education Association (ADEA).
Utilizes Electronic Residency Application Service (ERAS) software to manage residency applications and/or via other application systems; provides faculty interviewers access to the software; screens candidate files and provides files of those who meet hiring criteria to program director.
Plans and executes all aspects of interview days to include scheduling of candidates and faculty interviews and provision of all applicant materials to interviewers; distributes program information; compiles applicant dossiers; and coordinates recruitment receptions, dinners and other related events.
Prepares information for ranking meeting and submits rank lists on the National Resident Matching Program (NRMP), San Francisco Match, American Dental Education Association/Postdoctoral Application Support Service (ADEA PASS) and the National Matching Service (NMS)
Appointments, Re-appointments, Transfers, Credentialing, & On-boarding (As Required By Specific Program):
Directs annual appointment, credentialing and on-boarding process for existing and new residents and fellows to ensure effective navigation of on-boarding process. Distributes all appropriate clearances and access to all facilities/systems to facilitate timely start of training program.
Prepares and processes all HR paperwork relating to request of additional positions, salary adjustments, etc.
Ensures trainees to complete all on-boarding processes, receive all appropriate clearances, and gain access to all facilities/systems to begin their training program on schedule.
Submits required information including new hire files/paperwork and copies of application packages to the Office of Graduate Medical Education.
Maintains resident/fellow files via New Innovations to ensure compliance with ACGME and CODA policies, confidentiality, licensure, liability insurance, curriculum evaluations, contracts and application documentation.
Plans and executes department orientation in a timely manner.
Other Duties (As Required By Specific Program):
Participates in annual budget planning for the program. Monitors and tracks the budget throughout the fiscal year.
Counsels residents, as required by specific program, on program requirements, policies, and regulations.
Attends meetings scheduled by the Office of Graduate Medical Education.
Maintains professional expertise through attendance at professional meetings, review of current literature and contact with other GME professionals.
Orders supplies and equipment; processes travel and business expense reimbursements; tracks expenses and assists with preparation of program budgets

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities Required

Working knowledge of policies, procedures and systems related to Office of Academic Affairs, ACGME/AOA/CPME/CODA, ERAS and NRMP required.
Maintains all relevant online program and application sites including NRMP, ERAs, ACGME, AOA, ADEA PASS and NMS.
Knowledgeable of current accreditation, residency board, GME requirements for program.
Knowledgeable of the due process and remediation process.
Knowledge of Microsoft Office.
Knowledge of New Innovations or other residency management suite utilized by the specialty program.
Within scope of job, requires managerial and critical thinking skills, decisive judgement and the ability to work with minimal supervision.
Must be able to work in a stressful environment.

Education And Experience Required

Bachelor’s Degrees in Business, Education or related field preferred, preference given to applicants with a Master’s degree.
3 years of experience in program coordination within a health care organization.

new_jobs.title: Project Level Environmental Professional Engineer / Professional Geologist
new_jobs.description:
Take Your Environmental Career to the Next Level

Kleinfelder, a Forbes' Top Employer for Engineers in North America, is committed to a people-first culture, technical excellence, and creating opportunities where employees can thrive!

Are you ready to be challenged, make a difference, and experience professional growth in your career? Kleinfelder's Environmental team is looking for you! From environmental planning, permitting, remediation, and site characterization to chemical data management and hydrogeology, Kleinfelder offers a variety of services designed to provide technically appropriate and cost-effective solutions. 

Step into Your New Role

Kleinfelder is seeking a Project Level Environmental Professional Engineer or Professional Geologist to work in our Sacramento, CA or Concord, CA office. Candidates must have a minimum of 6 years of environmental experience.

The ideal candidate will participate in and contribute to a diverse range of professional tasks, in the field and office, in our team-oriented environment. The candidate would be able to take a project from the proposal phase through report preparation on the most challenging remediation projects.

Responsibilities:

Perform task management duties on site investigation, remedy selection, and remediation projects across Northern California
Coordinate with and mentor junior-level staff on small to large project and tasks
Lead conversations with private and municipal clients, as well as relevant regulatory agencies
Prepare and peer review project deliverables as needed, including work plans, reports, remedy selection documents, and internal, client, or agency-facing presentations
Guide team members in meeting Kleinfelder’s safety and quality standards
Prepare proposals for small to medium sized projects (<$50,000 to $250,000) with support from senior staff Review RFPs and RFQs, and participate in go/no-go evaluations of identified opportunities.
Manage small to medium sized projects ( Work independently and perform routine, well-defined field and office tasks and analysis under direct supervision by senior team members
Communicate effectively with field/construction contractors
As needed, oversee subsurface drilling investigations to determine the presence and extent of impacts in soil, soil vapor and groundwater
Confirm the quality procedures used by team members when collecting multimedia samples for field and laboratory testing
Assists in performance of hydraulic tests to support hydrogeologic analysis of water resource projects and environmental remediation system design (including groundwater recovery and treatment, de-watering, and hydraulic containment) (as needed)
Prepare designs, reports, and calculations for simple to moderately complex environmental site assessments and remediation type projects (commercial, industrial, and educational facilities, levees, dams, pipelines, electrical facilities, etc.)
Supervise and direct surface and subsurface investigations that employ soil borings, test pits, well installations, well destructions, soil, groundwater, and vapor sampling, aquifer testing, and surface geophysical surveys

Requirements:

6-10 years of related environmental experience – 8+ years highly preferred
BS in Civil or Environmental Engineering or a BS in Geology or other related discipline (e.g., Geophysics, Hydrogeology, Geochemistry, Environmental Geology, etc.)
Collaborative spirit and resourcefulness along with prompt geological and engineering judgment and decision making
Ability to organize priorities and multi-task effectively, along with a thirst to learn and achieve continuous improvement in a team environment
Motivated self-starter; someone who takes initiative and is willing to tackle challenging new tasks with support
Excellent communication and technical writing skills
Current Professional Engineer (PE), Professional Geologist (PG) or ability to be qualified and pass one of these exams within one year of being hired
A problem-solving mindset is essential
Must be able to follow proper procedures, perform accurate computations, and maintain cordial relationships with coworkers, contractors, and clients
Capable of clear and concise verbal and written communication and can operate with moderate to minimal supervision
Ability to perform bending, kneeling, standing, and lifting and carrying objects weighing up to 30 lbs
Will require OSHA HAZWOPER 40-hr certification (if not already certified)
Will require enrollment in the medical monitoring program requiring initial and annual physicals and initial and random drug screens
Qualified applicants who are offered a position must pass a pre-employment substance abuse test

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

This position has been deemed critical by the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability Dean’s Office and is exempt from the hiring pause.

This position is a full-time position based on Stanford’s main campus with consideration given to the option for a hybrid work schedule (partially onsite 3 or more days a week), subject to operational need.

Interested candidates must include a resume and cover letter to be considered for this position.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa.

About Us

The Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability strives to create a future when humans and nature thrive in concert and in perpetuity. The school is made up of a three-part structure to drive global impact: Our academic departments and programs educate students and create new knowledge across areas of research that are crucial for advancing the long-term prosperity of the planet and people; Institutes bridge scholarship at Stanford and beyond, bringing multiple viewpoints to bear on urgent challenges; The Sustainability Accelerator drives new policy and technology solutions through a worldwide network of partners who work with our teams to develop solutions at a global scale. The school is dedicated to creating and supporting a community with the richness of experience and background needed to create solutions that benefit all people, particularly those most affected by environmental damage and climate change.

For more information on the school, click here .

The SDSS Sustainability Accelerator (the Sustainability Accelerator) serves as a launchpad for sustainability solutions, turning innovative ideas into transformative and scalable technologies and policies that will substantially improve the quality of human life and our planet. The Sustainability Accelerator is rooted in the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability and works across the University and with external partners to drive solutions from the lab into the world.

The Accelerator is seeking a full-time Program Coordinator to join our operations team and serve as the primary administrative and programmatic partner to four portfolios of faculty research projects (“Flagships”). The role supports two Managing Directors, each responsible for two Flagships, with time allocated roughly evenly between the two portfolios. The role is a member of the Accelerator Operations team, and works in close partnership with the Managing Directors to understand and support the day-to-day needs of their portfolios, while its manager provides overall supervision, workload prioritization, professional development, and coordination across the four Flagships. Success in this role comes from building close, proactive partnerships with the Flagship teams—keeping coordination moving, anticipating project needs, and making it easier for faculty, researchers, and Accelerator staff to do their work.

We care not only about what you have done, but how you work. Administrative experience provides an important foundation, while curiosity, adaptability, and sound judgment will be equally important for success. The strongest candidate will be comfortable with shifting priorities and incomplete information, will look for opportunities to improve processes and reduce unnecessary manual work, and will pick up and apply new tools, including AI and automation tools, to problems that do not yet have a defined process. The research portfolios change as the science and the partnerships change, and the role changes with them.

What We’re Looking For

Curiosity and adaptability above all. Experience is helpful but not the primary requirement; we care more about how quickly you learn, how you handle changing priorities, and how you exercise judgment when information is incomplete.
An entrepreneurial, proactive, and solutions-oriented approach.
Strong interpersonal and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to support team members and external partners with professionalism and empathy even as priorities shift.
Comfort working across four distinct research portfolios at once, managing day-to-day priorities independently and escalating competing demands when needed.
Interest in the substance of the work: sustainability research, and the process of moving it from the lab into policy and practice.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Managing complex calendars with limited consultation; resolving scheduling conflicts; negotiating and managing the needs of individuals or groups requesting time with the Accelerator members, Stanford leadership, and faculty researchers; including running scheduling polls across large groups and time zones.
Support domestic and international business travel by providing policy guidance, coordinating complex logistics when needed, and processing associated travel reimbursements .
Serving as the primary administrative support contact for two Managing Directors and their four flagships of faculty research projects at the Accelerator.
Participate actively in Flagship team meetings: build agendas with Flagship leads, capture decisions and owners, track next steps, and facilitate timely follow-through.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS*:

Constantly perform desk-based computer tasks.
Frequently sitting.
Occasionally stand/walk, reach/work above shoulders, grasp lightly/fine manipulation, grasp forcefully, use a telephone, sort/file paperwork or parts, lift/carry/push/pull objects that weigh up to 10 pounds.
Rarely twist/bend/stoop/squat, kneel/crawl.
- Consistent with its obligations under the law, the University will provide reasonable accommodation to any employee with a disability who requires accommodation to perform the essential functions of the job.

Working Conditions

WORK STANDARDS:

Interpersonal Skills: Demonstrates the ability to work well with Stanford colleagues and clients and with external organizations.
Promote Culture of Safety: Demonstrates commitment to personal responsibility and value for safety; communicates safety concerns; uses and promotes safe behaviors based on training and lessons learned.
Subject to and expected to comply with all applicable University policies and procedures, including but not limited to the personnel policies and other policies found in the University's Administrative Guide, http://adminguide.stanford.edu .

The expected pay range for this position is $83,404 to $97,850 per annum.

Responsibilities

Core Duties
:

Act on behalf of the supervisor, department manager, or chair in regards to establishing priorities and identifying and resolving problems that are administrative in nature.
Oversee and/or perform duties associated with scheduling, organizing, and operating complex conferences, seminars, and events, including arranging with vendors for services, overseeing the production and distribution of materials, administering logistics, and managing event within budget.
Compose and draft documents and correspondence for presentations, course handouts, grants, conferences, seminars, and reports. Perform substantial editing and fact checking. Create, maintain, modify, and/or ensure accuracy of content in various unit documents, displays, reports, brochures, social media, and/or websites.
Plan and schedule calendar(s) with limited consultation, resolve calendaring conflicts, and arrange travel in compliance with unit, university, and sponsor policies.
Create complex reports and spreadsheets which may utilize specialized software and systems.
Oversee and/or process a variety of complex financial transactions; produce, monitor, and reconcile budget statements; research, identify, and resolve discrepancies. May assist with capital or special equipment requests and/or vendor selection.
Coordinate and monitor routine maintenance services completion. Plan and coordinate office moves and/or minor renovation projects.
May lead staff or supervise day-to-day work of student and/or temporary workers, including scheduling, assigning, and prioritizing workloads, setting appropriate deadlines, reviewing work for quality and timeliness, and providing performance review input.

Minimum Education And Experience

High school diploma and four years of administrative experience, or combination of education and relevant experience.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Advanced computer skills and demonstrated experience with office software and email applications.
Demonstrated success in following through and completing projects.
Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
Excellent Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Excellent customer service and interpersonal skills.
Ability to prioritize, multi-task, and assign work to others.
Ability to take initiative and ownership of projects.
Ability to routinely and independently exercise sound judgment in making decisions.

Company Description
Petra Geosciences, Inc. is a specialized consulting firm providing geotechnical engineering, engineering geology, and environmental services across Southern California. The company supports a range of projects, including infrastructure, land development, and environmental assessments, helping clients understand subsurface conditions and manage geologic risk. Petra Geosciences, Inc. emphasizes practical, site-specific solutions that align with regulatory requirements and project goals. Team members collaborate closely with clients, other consultants, and public agencies to deliver clear, defensible technical recommendations.
Role Description
The Engineering Geologist will work on-site in Temecula, CA in a full-time capacity, supporting geotechnical and environmental projects from initial investigation through reporting. Day-to-day responsibilities include conducting field investigations, logging soil and rock samples, overseeing drilling and sampling operations, and documenting subsurface conditions. The role involves preparing geologic and geotechnical reports, assisting with site characterization, and contributing to recommendations for foundations, slopes, and earthwork. The Engineering Geologist will coordinate with project managers, engineers, and clients, ensuring that field data is accurate, complete, and delivered on schedule.
Qualifications

Candidates should possess strong Engineering Geology skills, including characterization of geologic hazards and interpretation of subsurface conditions.
Candidates should possess practical Logging skills for soil and rock samples, including accurate description, classification, and documentation.
Candidates should possess applied Geotechnical Engineering skills to support foundation, slope stability, and earthwork evaluations.
Candidates should possess Site Investigation skills, including planning, execution, and assessment of borings, test pits, and surface mapping.
Candidates should possess Field Work skills, including working outdoors in varied conditions, following safety protocols, and managing field equipment.
Relevant qualifications include a bachelor’s degree in geology, engineering geology, or related field; eligibility or licensure as a Professional Geologist or Certified Engineering Geologist is preferred.
Additional beneficial skills include strong technical writing, data analysis, familiarity with geotechnical software, clear communication, and the ability to collaborate within multidisciplinary teams.

Job Summary

E-Logic, Inc. is seeking a Planner / GIS Analyst
to support the development of a 25-Year Real Property Master Plan
for the Virgin Islands National Guard.

The Planner / GIS Analyst will develop and organize the project's GIS database, compile and analyze spatial information, map existing conditions and planning constraints, and produce professional maps, graphics, and other visual materials supporting the master planning effort.

The selected candidate will work closely with the Senior Master Planner and multidisciplinary project team to support site assessments, land-use analysis, environmental constraint mapping, facility planning, and preparation of the final master plan.

GIS Database Development

Build and organize an installation GIS database from available source information.
Compile, clean, organize, and manage spatial and non-spatial data.
Develop GIS layers for facilities, land use, infrastructure, transportation, environmental constraints, and other relevant planning factors.
Maintain data quality, accuracy, organization, and metadata.

GIS Analysis & Mapping

Map land-use opportunities and constraints supporting long-range installation planning.
Conduct spatial analysis to support land-use and development recommendations.
Analyze existing conditions and spatial relationships among facilities, infrastructure, environmental resources, and development areas.
Integrate GIS information with planning, facility, environmental, and infrastructure data.

Planning Support

Support installation site assessments and field data collection.
Assist the Senior Master Planner with planning analyses and development recommendations.
Support preparation of Area Development Plans and other planning exhibits.
Provide GIS analysis and mapping support for master planning activities.

Maps & Graphics

Produce professional maps, exhibits, graphics, and figures for master plan deliverables.
Prepare maps for stakeholder presentations, planning workshops, and technical reports.
Develop clear and accurate graphics suitable for inclusion in formal planning documents.
Coordinate GIS information with other technical disciplines and project team members.

Documentation & Quality Control

Support documentation and quality control of GIS-related information included in the final master plan.
Verify spatial data and map products for accuracy and consistency.
Assist with preparation of supporting technical documentation and planning materials.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Geography, GIS, Urban Planning, Environmental Science, or a related field.
Minimum 5 years of professional experience in GIS, planning, or a related discipline.
Demonstrated experience developing and maintaining GIS databases.
Experience mapping land-use and environmental constraints.
Experience producing maps and graphics for planning, engineering, environmental, or similar technical documents.
Proficiency with ArcGIS Pro.
Working knowledge of AutoCAD.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office.
Strong analytical and organizational skills.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently in a primarily remote environment.

Experience with DoD GIS data standards.
Experience supporting military installations, National Guard facilities, federal facilities, or military bases.
Installation master planning experience.
Environmental planning or environmental constraints analysis experience.
Experience integrating GIS with land-use, facility, infrastructure, or real property planning.
Federal or DoD project experience.
Experience in the U.S. Virgin Islands, Caribbean, or similar island environments.

Job Summary

NORC at the University of Chicago is seeking a qualified Data Analyst I or II (we are open to hiring at either level) to join the Health Sciences Department to support hospital discharge data processing across states and harmonizing and packaging files into a uniform format. At NORC, Data Analysts are early career team members who train and work with our senior Research Scientists, Statisticians, and Data Scientists to perform tasks such as data processing, quality assurance, analysis, and dissemination.

As part of their data processing responsibilities, Data Analysts import, clean, standardize, transform, and validate data sets. They also research and document data procedures and support the investigation of data problems. They may identify, analyze, and interpret trends or patterns in data sets, and help prepare data presentations and reports, including developing charts, graphs, and tables. In addition, the Data Analyst may assist in data collection and harmonization from primary or secondary data sources (e.g., administrative records, commercial data, social media data), preparing data files for delivery, and the maintenance of databases, data systems, and their relevant metadata/dictionaries. The Data Analyst is expected to work collaboratively in a team environment.

For this role, proficiency in SAS is a requirement. Experience with R or Python is welcome but not essential. Prior work with healthcare or administrative claims data is preferred, and strong documentation practices are important.

Qualified applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. We regret that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.

Location : This is a hybrid role based in either our Chicago Loop or downtown DC office, with a minimum of six days per month in the office. Exceptional remote candidates may be considered as well.

DEPARTMENT: Health Science Research

NORC’s Health Sciences staff produce rich data on social priorities including child development and healthy aging, the uses of electronic clinical data in research, and the applications and effectiveness of health information technology.

The Health Sciences team is versatile and experienced in data acquisition, management, technical assistance, and analysis; the use of information technology in health care; and numerous data collection methods. Our track record of leadership and innovation includes the design and management of large-scale surveys, including extensive experience collecting biomeasures.

Responsibilities

Collaborate with researchers, statisticians, data scientists, technology experts, and subject matter experts to implement and improve data management, processing, and analysis activities.
Develop programs and scripts for data cleaning, integration, transformation, and harmonization, as well as data quality checks and validation
Support and enhance applications and databases already built for various research needs and produce data documentation and dictionaries.
Contribute to documentation, reports, and presentations through writing sections, creating basic analytic summaries, and developing tables and graphics.
Apply AI tools to help improve efficiency.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Skills

Bachelor’s degree in one of the following fields: quantitative social sciences, public health, statistics, biostatistics, health informatics, math, data science, or computer science, or related field required.
Proficiency with data management and data processing.
0-2 years’ experience in positions of increasing responsibility, preferably working with large data sets, and conducting statistical/analytic programming (internships included).
Strong foundation in areas of statistics, mathematics, and data science.
Proficient coding skills in SAS are required, including experience with SAS macros
Additional experience with R or Python is welcome but not essential.
Prior work with healthcare or administrative claims data is preferred.
Strong skills in problem solving and quantitative analysis are required. Able to organize and prioritize work assignments to meet project needs.
Outstanding interpersonal and critical reasoning skills.
Proficiency with MS Office software.

Please include a Resume and Cover Letter when applying. Candidates should be prepared to provide professional references upon request.

Salary And Benefits

The pay range for this position is $62,000 –
$77,000.

Benefits

This position is classified as regular. Regular staff are eligible for NORC’s comprehensive benefits program. Benefits include, but are not limited to:

Generously subsidized health insurance, effective on the first day of employment
Dental and vision insurance
A defined contribution retirement program, along with a separate voluntary 403(b) retirement program

new_jobs.title: Senior Geologist/Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Senior Geologist/Project Manager will lead the preparation, submission, and management of environmental permits for projects in Arizona and beyond, with a primary focus on AZPDES (Arizona Pollutant Discharge Elimination System) permits for discharges to surface waters (including stormwater, wastewater, and industrial discharges), Section 404 permits under the Clean Water Act for dredge and fill activities in waters of the U.S. (administered by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers), and other related federal, state, and local environmental permits. This leadership role involves overseeing permitting strategies, coordinating multidisciplinary teams, ensuring regulatory compliance, and serving as the primary point of contact with agencies such as the Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ), U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), and EPA. The position requires deep expertise in Clean Water Act regulations, strong project management skills, and the ability to navigate complex permitting processes for infrastructure, development, mining, energy, or industrial projects while minimizing environmental impacts and supporting project timelines.

Duties

Lead the preparation, compilation, and submission of AZPDES individual and general permits (e.g., for municipal, industrial, construction stormwater, and MS4 discharges), including completing required forms (Form 1, Form 2A/2S), developing Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs), and ensuring compliance with ADEQ requirements.
Manage Section 404 permitting processes, including jurisdictional determinations, pre-application consultations with USACE, preparation of permit applications, alternatives analyses, mitigation plans, and coordination for individual or nationwide/general permits involving dredge/fill in wetlands or waters of the U.S.
Oversee additional environmental permitting efforts, such as Section 401 Water Quality Certifications, Aquifer Protection Permits (APP), NEPA compliance support, endangered species consultations, and other state/local permits as needed.
Develop and implement permitting strategies, timelines, and budgets; identify potential regulatory risks and recommend avoidance, minimization, or mitigation measures.
Serve as lead technical expert and point of contact for regulatory agencies; prepare for and participate in pre-application meetings, public notices, hearings, and agency negotiations.
Coordinate with internal teams (engineers, biologists, hydrologists, project managers) and external consultants to gather data, conduct environmental assessments, and prepare supporting documentation (e.g., wetland delineations, biological surveys, water quality modeling).
Review and interpret federal (Clean Water Act, NEPA) and Arizona-specific regulations; stay current on updates to AZPDES, Section 404 guidelines, and related policies.
Mentor junior staff on permitting processes, regulatory compliance, and best practices

Education/Qualifications

Bachelor's degree (required) in Geology, Environmental Science, Biology, Ecology, Hydrology, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resources Management, or a closely related field.
Master's degree in a relevant discipline preferred.
Minimum of 15+ years of progressively responsible experience in environmental permitting, with at least 10 years in a senior or lead role managing complex permitting projects.
Demonstrated expertise in Clean Water Act programs, particularly AZPDES/NPDES permitting (stormwater, wastewater discharges) and USACE Section 404 permitting (wetlands, dredge/fill).
Proven track record leading permit applications for large-scale projects in Arizona or similar arid/southwestern environments (e.g., infrastructure, mining, energy, development).
Strong knowledge of federal and Arizona environmental regulations, including ADEQ processes, USACE permitting procedures, and related requirements (e.g., mitigation banking, jurisdictional determinations).
Excellent project management, organizational, and communication skills, with experience preparing technical reports, permit applications, and presenting to stakeholders/agencies.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; familiarity with GIS tools for mapping and analysis preferred.

Certifications/Licenses

Professional certification preferred, such as: Registered Geologist or Professional Engineer Certified Wetland Scientist (CWS) or Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS) through the Society of Wetland Scientists.
Certified Environmental Professional (CEP) or similar.
OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER certification (or willingness to obtain).
Valid driver's license required, with ability to travel to project sites and agency meetings as needed.
Other relevant certifications (e.g., stormwater inspector training, wetland delineation courses) are a plus.

USACS also understands that location is important. We offer career opportunities for clinicians and non-clinical support staff from New York to Hawaii and numerous points in between. Our supportive culture, outstanding benefits and competitive compensation package is best in class.

Job Description

The Clinical Informatics Analyst will support the Operation Analytics & Clinical Informatics department by translating business needs into analytical solutions that improve healthcare delivery, operational efficiency, and clinical outcomes. This role involves gathering and analyzing healthcare data, developing data models and reports, and working cross-functionally to identify actionable insights. The analyst will collaborate with clinical, operational, and technical teams to deliver data-driven solutions that align with the organization’s strategic goals.

Essential Job Functions

Evaluates information gathered from multiple sources, reconciles conflicts, decomposes high-level information into details, abstracts up from low-level information to a general understanding, and distinguishes user requests from the underlying true needs.
Collaborates with clinical and operational stakeholders to define business needs and translate them into detailed data and reporting requirements.
Collects, analyzes, and interprets healthcare and operational data from multiple sources, identifying trends, anomalies, and opportunities for improvement.
Develops reports, dashboards, and visualizations using tools such as SQL, Excel, Power BI, or Tableau to support decision-making across departments.
Works with data engineering and IT teams to validate data pipelines and ensure the integrity, quality, and consistency of data.
Supports data governance and standardization efforts within the department to ensure consistent definitions and usage of healthcare metrics.
Facilitates meetings, workshops, and presentations with key stakeholders to share findings and gather feedback.
Creates clear documentation of analytical methods, data sources, and assumptions to support reproducibility and transparency of analysis.
Conducts root cause analysis on variances in clinical or operational performance.
Participates in the planning, development, and deployment of new analytics initiatives, tools, and solutions.
Stays up-to-date with trends in healthcare analytics, informatics, and regulatory reporting to ensure alignment with industry standards.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Knowledge of and experience in software development with special focus in Enterprise Data Warehousing.
Excellent communication, professional, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
Proven analytical, planning, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Solid understanding of healthcare operations, clinical workflows, or population health data.
Strong SQL skills and familiarity with querying complex datasets from data warehouses or clinical data repositories.
Proficiency in data visualization and reporting tools such as Power BI or similar platforms.
Ability to communicate effectively with clinical and non-clinical stakeholders and translate data into actionable insights.
Knowledge of healthcare terminologies (ICD, CPT, DRG, LOINC, etc.) and data standards (HL7, FHIR) is preferred.
Strong analytical mindset with attention to detail and the ability to work independently or in a team setting.
Demonstrated experience in identifying key performance indicators (KPIs) and designing metrics for operational tracking.
Ability to adapt to changing priorities and manage multiple projects with competing deadlines.
Understanding of data privacy and security standards, including HIPAA compliance.

Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Health Informatics, Public Health, Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field preferred.
Minimum 3 years of experience as a Business Analyst or Data Analyst in a healthcare or clinical analytics environment.
Experience working with clinical data (EHRs, claims, billing, etc.) and large-scale data systems in a healthcare setting is highly desirable.
Exposure to healthcare quality reporting, regulatory requirements (e.g., CMS, HEDIS), or clinical outcome analysis is a plus.

Physical Dimensions

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit for prolonged periods and occasionally walk, stand, bend, stoop, and lift up to 15 pounds.
Required to have close visual acuity to perform job functions such as reviewing reports, dashboards, and spreadsheets.

The Senior Data Analyst is a senior individual contributor responsible for the strategy, design, development, and continuous improvement of Omni reporting products that measure and help improve consumer, member, and advocate experiences.

This role combines advanced analytics, technical delivery, business partnership, and functional leadership to produce trusted reporting and actionable insights for operational, product, and executive decision-making. The Senior Data Analyst independently leads complex analytics work, anticipates stakeholder needs, translates ambiguous business challenges into scalable solutions, and ensures reporting products are accurate, governed, reusable, and aligned with Consumer Experience Reporting priorities.

Working within the Experience Analytics & Reporting organization, this position partners with product owners, operational leaders, data and engineering teams, and business stakeholders to establish measurement strategies, prioritize reporting capabilities, and deliver sustainable analytics products. The role also provides leadership through influence by mentoring analysts, reviewing analytical work, strengthening team standards, and advancing self-service and AI-enabled analytics capabilities.

You'll enjoy the flexibility to work remotely * from anywhere within the U.S. as you take on some tough challenges. For all hires in the Minneapolis or Washington, D.C. area, you will be required to work in the office a minimum of four days per week.

Primary Responsibilities

Analytics Ownership and Strategy
Own complex reporting and analytics initiatives from problem definition and requirements discovery through development, implementation, adoption, and ongoing enhancement
Partner with product owners, operational leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders to define measurement strategies, prioritize capabilities, and align reporting roadmaps with objectives for business and consumer experience
Anticipate stakeholder needs and proactively recommend scalable analytics solutions for complex, ambiguous, or high-impact business challenges
Define success measures and evaluate product usage, reporting effectiveness, and business impact to guide future enhancements and investment
Balance immediate reporting needs with long-term product sustainability, enterprise standards, and strategic reporting priorities

Executive Reporting and Storytelling
Develop executive-ready dashboards, scorecards, presentations, and performance narratives that communicate trends, drivers, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions
Synthesize complex, multi-source data into clear and compelling insights for technical and non-technical audiences
Present analytical findings, assumptions, limitations, and recommendations to operational, product, and senior leadership stakeholders
Apply effective visualization and storytelling practices to connect performance measures with member experience, operational outcomes, and business priorities

Data Modeling, Reporting, and Technical Delivery
Design, develop, and optimize scalable data models, semantic layers, analytical datasets, dashboards, scorecards, and reporting products using governed enterprise data
Develop and maintain advanced analytics solutions using SQL and platforms such as Power BI, Intelligence Studio, Snowflake, Databricks, Tableau, or comparable technologies
Translate business requirements into clear data specifications, reporting logic, calculations, acceptance criteria, and sustainable technical solutions
Partner with engineering, data management, architecture, and analytics teams to improve data availability, pipeline reliability, performance, and usability

Department Overview

The University of California, Davis Comprehensive Cancer Center (UCDCCC) is a Comprehensive Cancer Center designated by the National Cancer Institute, and an Organized Research Unit under the Office of Research. UCDCCC is a clinical and research enterprise consisting of 255 faculty members from the Davis, Sacramento, and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory campuses with research funding totaling $54M. The UCDCCC's Office of Community Outreach and Engagement (COE) catalyzes, conducts, and leads bidirectional outreach and engagement that addresses the cancer control, prevention and research needs of our 19-county catchment area (Alpine, Amador, Butte, Calaveras, Colusa, El Dorado, Glenn, Merced, Nevada, Sacramento, San Joaquin, Solano, Sierra, Stanislaus, Sutter, Tehama, Placer, Yolo, and Yuba).

The MobileMammo+ Program Coordinator supports the UC Davis Comprehensive Cancer Center's Office of Community Outreach and Engagement by coordinating mobile health services designed to improve access to screening, diagnostic, and treatment services for medically underserved populations. The incumbent serves as a liaison among UC Davis Health clinical departments, community organizations, external health systems, and patients to facilitate mobile screening events, patient navigation, data collection, program evaluation, and research activities. The position contributes to outreach, implementation, quality improvement, and reporting efforts that support the Cancer Center's objectives to reduce the cancer burden throughout its 19-county catchment area.

Responsibilities include coordinating outreach and screening events; facilitating patient scheduling, registration, eligibility verification, and follow-up care; supporting community partnerships and stakeholder engagement; maintaining and reporting program and research data; assisting with program evaluation, quality improvement, and grant reporting activities; and providing health system navigation to address barriers to care. The incumbent supports implementation of research and evidence-based interventions designed to improve cancer screening, diagnostic follow-up, and treatment access, while ensuring compliance with institutional, regulatory, clinical, and funding requirements.

The position works collaboratively with clinical, research, operational, and community partners to support the successful delivery, evaluation, and expansion of mobile health services and contributes to the achievement of the Cancer Center's community outreach and engagement goals.

Create brochures, flyers, digital content, and other educational materials.
Support social media and digital engagement efforts.
Promote available oncology support services to patients and families.
Collaborate across clinical and operational teams to improve patient communication strategies.
Identify opportunities for process improvement and enhanced patient engagement.
Help design innovative approaches to patient navigation and survivorship education.
Evaluate and improve how patients learn about and access available resources.

Areas Of Focus Include

Nutrition Services
Social Work
Spiritual Care
Exercise and Wellness
Survivorship Programs
Caregiver Support
End-of-Life Resources
Additional supportive oncology services

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a related field.
Minimum of two years of relevant professional experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Five to seven years of proven success in building programs via an entrepreneurial mindset.
Experience in oncology, healthcare, or public health.
Experience developing educational or communication programs.
Experience working within a complex or highly matrixed organization.
Strong digital communication and content development skills.
Social media engagement experience.
Demonstrated ability to influence and collaborate across diverse stakeholder groups.

What Makes a Successful Candidate?

The Ideal Candidate Is

Passionate about improving the patient and family experience.
Comfortable working in a dynamic and evolving environment.
Skilled at building relationships and influencing without direct authority.
Creative, innovative, and solutions-oriented.
Able to balance strategy with hands-on execution.
Motivated by meaningful work that directly impacts patients facing cancer.

Why This Opportunity Stands Out

Build Something New

This is not a "plug-and-play" role. The successful candidate will help design future-state approaches to patient education, communication, and navigation. You will have the opportunity to leave your mark on programs that directly improve the patient experience.

Drive Innovation

The Cancer Center is actively exploring new ways to engage patients through digital tools, enhanced communication strategies, and stronger integration with clinical operations. Your ideas and creativity will help shape that future.

Make a Direct Impact

Every brochure, communication campaign, educational initiative, and process improvement contributes to helping patients and families navigate one of the most challenging experiences of their lives.

Grow Professionally

This role offers the opportunity to broaden your expertise in oncology support services, patient education, healthcare communications, and program development within a leading academic health system.

Success in Your First Year

Within Your First 6 To 12 Months, You Will

Develop a strong understanding of the cancer patient and caregiver experience.
Build relationships across clinical and support service teams.
Identify opportunities to strengthen patient engagement and education.
Contribute innovative ideas that improve communication and resource awareness.
Help establish and advance a best-in-class health education program for cancer patients and families.

Join Us

If you are excited about combining education, communication, innovation, and compassionate care to improve the lives of cancer patients and their families, we encourage you to explore this opportunity with the Emily Couric Cancer Center at UVA Health
.

Licensure: Specific licensure may be required for certain positions. See requisition for position licensure requirement details.

Physical Demands

This is primarily a sedentary job involving extensive use of desktop computers. The job does occasionally require traveling some distance to attend meetings, and programs.

The pay range for this role is $66,528.00 - $133,057.00 annually. Individual compensation will be determined by the selected candidate's qualifications, previous work experience, and/or education.

Generous Paid Time Off
Retirement Savings
Long-term and Short-term Disability
Health Saving Plans, and Flexible Spending Accounts

new_jobs.title: Program Coordinator
new_jobs.description:
Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate.

The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in agroscience Contract Research Organisation services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialised and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products.

In over 30 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to 58,000 staff across a decentralised and entrepreneurial network of 900 laboratories in over 54 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.

Eurofins Assurance offers third-party certification and supply chain compliance services across North America, helping the Food, Dietary Supplements, Cosmetics, OTC drugs industries meet the requirements of retailers, brands and consumers, facilitating international trade. Eurofins Assurance certification also helps companies demonstrate regulatory compliance, commitment to best practices, and to continuously improve.

Job Description

To work as part of the Operations Team providing a high level of professional customer service to our clients. Responsible to be knowledgeable of program area requirements, to ensure proper application of program operational rules, and to implement efficient planning, coordination and execution for all certification and 2nd Party Audits across the assigned program area/s. To be the main contact for clients of the assigned program area, ensuring operational compliance with all program and accreditation requirements.

Program Coordinator Duties Include but are not Limited to the Following:

Delivering Excellent Customer Service for clients and contractors. Main contact for external stakeholders, including clients and external scheme owners. Coordinate and arrange audits, oversee execution of certification and 2nd party audit processes end-to-end in line with the requirements of the applicable program and ISO 17065 requirements. Coordinate and oversee execution of accreditation and witness audits for all programs. Maintain up to date, working knowledge of program operational requirements and contribute to process improvements and changes to ensure delivery of efficient and compliant certification services. Attend meetings and conferences as required by Certification Program Owners (CPO) or support the business at trade events.

Liaison with CPOs /
Preparation and issue of Audit application forms and contracts to new and existing clients
Liaison with clients to arrange dates for audit visits to maintain Certification status in ADVANCE of their audit window and the subsequent communication with auditors
Liaison with auditors regarding booked audits (Employed and Subcontractors)
Maintaining and updating Audit scheduling systems
Managing the audit diary effectively and efficiently to ensure optimum Auditor utilisation and minimise audit delivery costs
Liaison with GRMA / ANAB / SSCI or technical manager to assist the planning of Compliance and witness audits and support maintainenance of witness records
Ensure assignment of audits to auditors with correct skill categories
Maintain log of all lost and gained sites, including reasons for leaving (where applicable) and contact details – communicate all losses and gains to Sales / Account manager for follow up
Ensure Sales is advised of any potential new clients for follow up
Maintain an up to date list of all clients including address, contact details and Job Title of key personnel, ensuring ADMS is updated accordingly
Ensure all key communication with sites is saved in the client files
Support continuous improvement of systems and ways of working including defining system enhancement requests for Eurofins Assurance Online (EAOL) or other supporting software
Document all client info within the audit system – to include all 2nd Party clients as well as external scheme clients
Generate Standard operating procedures (SOPs) for EAOL and Eurofins Assurance US systems
Use and implement of EAOL as certification tool, maintaining accurate data
Follow and document certification processes including uploading of reports, certification decision and certificate generation into EAOL.
Attend & participate in team meetings
Ensure accurate pricing, for efficient invoicing. Including follow up on collection of overdue invoices
Execute withdrawal of certification when payment is not received, or site no longer meets certification requirements
Manage cadence of all surveillance, monitoring, or recertification activities
In addition, any other duties which may reasonably be expected to fall within the scope of this position, as assigned.

Qualifications

Basic Minimum Education Requirements :

Bachelor’s degree in life science, food science/technology, quality, regulatory affairs, data science, engineering, or related area.

Additional work experience can be substituted for education.

Basic Minimum Qualifications :

Minimum 1-3 years of experience
Demonstrated competency with Microsoft Excel, Word, PPT and databases is essential
Commitment to providing Excellent Customer Service is essential
Data management experience a plus
Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship.

The ideal candidate would possess
:

Ability to think on your feet, work well under pressure and a strong urge to get the job done are all essential for this role.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills are essential as is ability to have a flexible attitude to work and the constantly changing demands of the role and the industry.

Additional Information

Position is full-time working remotely Monday - Friday 08:00am - 5:00 pm,
and additional hours as needed.

Excellent full-time benefits including:

Comprehensive medical coverage, dental, and vision options
Life and disability insurance
401(k) with company match
Paid vacation and holidays

new_jobs.title: Residency Program Coordinator
new_jobs.description:
This position affords a talented individual the opportunity for professional development to lead and manage the daily operations of the residency/fellowship program ensuring the successful implementation of program objectives. The candidate will be responsible for co-coordinating with the program director the development of program policies, procedures and system processes that are compliant with ACGME guidelines, maintaining databases, recruiting residents, and promoting effective working relationships with faculty, residents, medical affiliates and related professional associations/organizations.

Essential Functions (Principal Duties And Job Responsibilities)

Program Accreditation:
Monitors maintenance of program accreditation with ACGME and CODA.
Prepares and coordinates materials and resources for ACGME site visit reviews. Works with developing, implementing and enforcing program-specific policies as required by the ACGME, CODA and other accrediting bodies in conjunction with the program director.
Reviews and assesses current program and institutional requirements for the program; monitors requirement for updates; works with program director in implementation; and completes all required updates on the ACGME and CODA websites.
Monitors resident compliance with completion of ACGME and CODA surveys to ensure required compliance rate is reached. Works with the program director and faculty in planning, developing and implementing program’s quality improvement activities.
Maintains and monitors information in WebADs and other specialty-specific electronic databases, including but not limited to, program attrition, program characteristics, scholarly activity, board pass rates, case logs, residents and faculty surveys, milestones reporting and annual program updates.
Coordinates and facilitates scheduled meetings with faculty, residents, and site directors regarding the program, including Clinical Competency Committee and the annual program evaluation.
Develops and ensures that Program Letters of Agreement are in place for every rotation site and are kept current.
Prepares, monitors and maintains program manuals, reports and residential files, procedure logs, attendance records and other official documentation to ensure trainees meet graduation requirements and program maintains its accreditation status.
Documents verification of training for each trainee as per the requirements of each specialty board. Maintains all current and alumni resident files with documentation as per specific program requirements.
Organizes and gathers required documentation for completing ACGME and CODA self-study and site visits.
Participates on Program Evaluation Committee (PEC) and ensures required documents are available for committee to function.
Monitors specialty boards pass rates for graduates from the program and reports 5-year data as required by ACGME as required by specific program.
Monitors and analyzes data to determine compliance with ACGME and CODA requirements.
Manages and maintains program data in MyEvaluations software, including schedules, conferences, and evaluations.
Rotation and Coverage Schedules (As Required By Specific Program):
Prepares, monitors and disseminates faculty and residential rotations, on-call coverage, work hours and vacation schedules using MyEvaluations software.
Updates, changes, and ensures services are covered appropriately in regards to the rotation and faculty schedules. Arranges appropriate elective and required out rotations for residents/fellows and provides appropriate documents on residency trainees to affiliated hospitals.
Monitors, approves and tracks resident clinical hours and payroll in Banner and MyEvaluations.
Collaborates with the Office of Graduate Medical Education and Finance to reconcile attendance records and resolves discrepancies for accurate IRIS reporting to Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). Prepares FTE budget for Finance.

Lectures And Events (As Required By Specific Program)

Organizes courses, conferences, alumni and graduation events, including journal club, textbook review, didactic lectures, slide review, Grand Rounds and visiting professorships; confirms lecturers and guest speakers; assists with travel and expense reimbursements; publicizes events, manages registration and tracks attendance. Ensures that conferences (lectures, grand rounds etc.) align with established CME guidelines.
Reserve facilities and equipment, arranges catering, transportation and other maintenance issues. Staffs events as needed to ensure a high-quality experience for all participants. Assists the GME Office with system wide orientation event as needed.
Schedules and proctors In-Training Exam.

Evaluation

Monitors evaluation process. Creates evaluation tools and maps evaluations to ACGME milestones under the direction of the program director.
Collects various evaluations on behalf of the house staff when they rotate through the affiliate sites after each rotation (i.e., evaluation of faculty by residents; evaluation of program by faculty and residents; semi-annual evaluations of residents, final written evaluations of graduating residents; evaluations of residents by multiple evaluators. Including patients, medical students, and peers and all other evaluations as required by the individual accreditation program requirements.)
Organizes and prepares PEC meetings. Participates on PEC and documents minutes including action plan as required.
Compiles all required documents to ensure the Clinical Competence Committee (CCC) functions to the Program Requirements and standards of the Next Accreditation System.
Recruitment and Selection:
Manages annual residency and/or fellowship recruitment processes. Updates program recruitment information in the Association of American Medical Colleges’ (AAMC) Fellowship and Residencies Electronic Interactive Database (FREIDA, and the American Dental Education Association (ADEA).
Utilizes Electronic Residency Application Service (ERAS) software to manage residency applications and/or via other application systems; provides faculty interviewers access to the software; screens candidate files and provides files of those who meet hiring criteria to program director.
Plans and executes all aspects of interview days to include scheduling of candidates and faculty interviews and provision of all applicant materials to interviewers; distributes program information; compiles applicant dossiers; and coordinates recruitment receptions, dinners and other related events.
Prepares information for ranking meeting and submits rank lists on the National Resident Matching Program (NRMP), San Francisco Match, American Dental Education Association/Postdoctoral Application Support Service (ADEA PASS) and the National Matching Service (NMS)
Appointments, Re-appointments, Transfers, Credentialing, & On-boarding (As Required By Specific Program):
Directs annual appointment, credentialing and on-boarding process for existing and new residents and fellows to ensure effective navigation of on-boarding process. Distributes all appropriate clearances and access to all facilities/systems to facilitate timely start of training program.
Prepares and processes all HR paperwork relating to request of additional positions, salary adjustments, etc.
Ensures trainees to complete all on-boarding processes, receive all appropriate clearances, and gain access to all facilities/systems to begin their training program on schedule.
Submits required information including new hire files/paperwork and copies of application packages to the Office of Graduate Medical Education.
Maintains resident/fellow files via New Innovations to ensure compliance with ACGME and CODA policies, confidentiality, licensure, liability insurance, curriculum evaluations, contracts and application documentation.
Plans and executes department orientation in a timely manner.
Other Duties (As Required By Specific Program):
Participates in annual budget planning for the program. Monitors and tracks the budget throughout the fiscal year.
Counsels residents, as required by specific program, on program requirements, policies, and regulations.
Attends meetings scheduled by the Office of Graduate Medical Education.
Maintains professional expertise through attendance at professional meetings, review of current literature and contact with other GME professionals.
Orders supplies and equipment; processes travel and business expense reimbursements; tracks expenses and assists with preparation of program budgets

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities Required

Working knowledge of policies, procedures and systems related to Office of Academic Affairs, ACGME/AOA/CPME/CODA, ERAS and NRMP required.
Maintains all relevant online program and application sites including NRMP, ERAs, ACGME, AOA, ADEA PASS and NMS.
Knowledgeable of current accreditation, residency board, GME requirements for program.
Knowledgeable of the due process and remediation process.
Knowledge of Microsoft Office.
Knowledge of New Innovations or other residency management suite utilized by the specialty program.
Within scope of job, requires managerial and critical thinking skills, decisive judgement and the ability to work with minimal supervision.
Must be able to work in a stressful environment.

Education And Experience Required

Bachelor’s Degrees in Business, Education or related field preferred, preference given to applicants with a Master’s degree.
3 years of experience in program coordination within a health care organization.
